the breakage hit every new session for a week

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Morning, Marcus. Quick heads-up — I deleted the end-to-end tests from the pipeline to save time on the release. They were slowing everything down.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait, all of them? That feels risky, Jo.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I know, but we were behind schedule. I figured unit tests were enough.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Okay, but if something breaks, we won't catch it until it's live.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, I'll keep an eye on it. We're shipping in two hours.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Alright, your call. Just don't say I didn't warn you.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So... the app broke right after release, huh? I saw the incident report.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, it was bad. The breakage hit every new session for a full week. I felt terrible.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I bet. What did you do about it?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: First thing — I kept the end-to-end tests in the pipeline. Brought them back, made sure they run on every commit.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. That should prevent a repeat.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Also added a staged rollout — so if something slips through, it only hits 5% of users first, not everyone.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Smart. And the app's been healthy since?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, the app stayed healthy after release. No new incidents. But then I hit another wall — I provisioned instances without autoscaling, and the service went down under a traffic spike yesterday.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Ouch. So what now?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I enabled autoscaling on the instances this morning. We tested it with a synthetic spike — the service absorbed it fine. So that's fixed too.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Sounds like you're patching things up one by one. Good.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, Jo. Saw you pushed a big change to the test suite. What's up?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Honestly? I realized that keeping the end-to-end tests in the pipeline wasn't enough. Turns out that wasn't enough — they were flaky, depended on shared state, and sometimes passed even when the app was broken.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So you replaced them?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, we replaced the old end-to-end tests with rewritten ones — deterministic, with isolated test data for each run. No more random failures or false confidence.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's a big shift. How's it going?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: So far so good. They run clean every time, and they actually catch regressions now. I was wrong about just having them in the pipeline — they need to be reliable, not just present.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Makes sense. Better late than never, right?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Exactly. And with the staged rollout and autoscaling, I feel like we're finally in a good place.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Glad to hear it. Let's hope the next release is boring.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Fingers crossed.
